newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FOWLER'S FIRST ENGLAND GOAL SEALS 2-0 WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FOWLER'S FIRST ENGLAND GOAL SEALS 2-0 WIN.

text.p: A dubious penalty decision and Robbie Fowler's first international goal gave England a 2-0 win over Mexico in a low-key friendly at Wembley on Saturday.
Tottenham forward Teddy Sheringham put Glenn Hoddle's side ahead from the spot after Mexico defender Pavel Pardo was adjudged to have tripped England captain Paul Ince in the box.

The decision appeared extremely harsh. Pardo had blocked a shot from Sheringham with a superb sliding tackle and caught Ince with the faintest of touches as he tried to clear the ball while still lying on the ground.
But Ince went down, the Portuguese referee pointed to the spot, and Sheringham slammed home his sixth goal of his England career and his second in three matches.
"I didn't think it was a penalty but I wasn't dressed in black with a whistle in my hand," Hoddle said. I haven't looked at it again but my instant reaction was that it wasn't a penalty."
Asked what he thought of the decision, Mexico coach Bora Milutinovic said: "I never like to speak against referees but it's important that you asked me. I think you know the answer."

England, forced by a large number of injuries into making changes to the side which lost 1-0 to Italy here last month, composed themselves as the half went on with Newcastle's Robert Lee and Liverpool's Steve McManaman impressive in midfield.
Mexico had their fair share of possession but were ineffectual in and around the England penalty area.
Lee forced a save from Aldolfo Rios with a crisp volley from a corner after half an hour and Claudio Suarez came close for Mexico with a header just before halftime.
Nine minutes after the break England doubled their lead.
Left-back Graeme Le Saux swung in a first time cross to the back post, Ian Wright powered a header goalwards, and when Rios parried, Fowler nipped in to head the ball into the net.
The goal will come as a tremendous relief for the 21-year- old, who has never reproduced his Liverpool form on the rare occasions he has been given the chance to play for England.
He now has to hope he can cling to his place when England play their next World Cup match against Georgia in a month's time.

"It was very important, Robbie Fowler getting off the mark in international football. It's a burden off his shoulders. It's important for a striker. He won't have that pressure next time and that's half the battle."

Mexico played their best football of the evening after they fell 2-0 behind, with captain Alberto Garcia Aspe and Marcelino Bernal almost embarrassing England's debutant keeper David James with long range efforts.
But England never looked like throwing away a victory which will go some way to restoring confidence badly shaken by the Italy defeat.
